page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.6xlarge is a member of the Local SSDs instance family, configured specifically for workloads demanding direct-attached solid-state disk storage alongside balanced compute and memory capacity. Built on the KVM hypervisor and an x86_64 architecture, this instance is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It offers 24 dedicated vCPUs paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core.

A primary architectural characteristic of the ecs.i1.6xlarge is its bundled local storage configuration. The instance incorporates 1340 GB of integrated SSD storage, eliminating reliance on remote network-attached disks for high-throughput primary data storage. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. The server does not contain dedicated GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing external traffic handling to associated cloud networking services.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of direct-attached local SSD capacity offers distinct resource density benefits for I/O-heavy environments. Workloads avoid the separate throughput quotas and pricing structures associated with cloud block storage volumes. However, tradeoffs inherent to local storage configurations include data persistence limitations, where storage lifecycle is directly bound to the virtual machine lifecycle.

The ecs.i1.6xlarge is engineered primarily for I/O-intensive workloads, including relational database engines, NoSQL datastores, real-time log analytics, search engine index processing, and distributed data processing frameworks requiring fast intermediate scratch space.
